nodes.title: The Segal E∞-monoid N(C) of a symmetric monoidal groupoid
nodes.statement: For a symmetric monoidal groupoid C and a finite pointed set (S, s), N(C)(S) is the nerve of the groupoid of families (X_T)_{T ⊆ S∖{s}} of objects of C with an isomorphism X_∅ ≅ 1 and compatible isomorphisms X_{T⊔T′} ≅ X_T ⊗ X_{T′} for disjoint T, T′ (compatible with the unit, associativity and symmetry constraints); a pointed map f : (S, s) → (S′, s′) sends (X_T) to (X_{f⁻¹(T′)})_{T′}. This is a strict functor Fin_* → Kan complexes and a special Γ-space with π₀ N(C) = C/≅ (Bhatt–Scholze Construction 12.5, with the nullary unit condition added).
hypotheses: C a symmetric monoidal groupoid; the unit condition X_∅ ≅ 1 is required (Bhatt–Scholze omit it: the known issue PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/E54).
proofSteps: Define the groupoid of coherent families and the functoriality by preimages, a strict functor (Bhatt–Scholze Construction 12.5).

The Segal map N(C)([n]) → N(C)^n, (X_T) ↦ (X_{{1}}, …, X_{{n}}), is an equivalence of groupoids: a family is determined up to unique isomorphism by its singletons, using the symmetric monoidal axioms (Mac Lane's coherence theorem for symmetric monoidal categories; Mathlib has only monoidal coherence, so this is the packet gap 'Symmetric monoidal coherence'); nerves of groupoids are Kan (H.1/groupoid-nerve-kan).
π₀ = isomorphism classes with ⊗ (Bhatt–Scholze proof of Proposition 12.15).
acceptance: For C = Vect(R) under ⊕, N(C) is the E∞-monoid whose group completion is the K-theory space of R.
For C = Pic(R) under ⊗, N(C) is already grouplike.

nodes.title: Segal's delooping theorem for special Γ-spaces
nodes.statement: For a special Γ-space X, let BX be the realisation of the simplicial space obtained by restricting X along Segal's functor Δ^op → Fin_*, [m] ↦ [m]; BX carries a special Γ-space structure and there is a natural map X → ΩBX. If X is k-connected then BX is (k+1)-connected; X → ΩBX is a weak equivalence iff X is grouplike; π₀(ΩBX) = π₁(BX) is the group completion of π₀(X); and for grouplike X the sequence X, BX, B²X, … is a connective Ω-spectrum.
hypotheses: X special; realisations of simplicial spaces as in H.2/simplicial-space-realisation.
proofSteps: Segal 1974, Proposition 1.4 (quoted by Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 12.10); its proof is not read (packet gap 'Infinite loop space machine equivalence'). The ingredient is H.2/levelwise-fibration-realisation applied to the simplicial path fibration; the homology group-completion statement is H.4/segal-group-completion-homology.
π₀(ΩBX) = π₁(BX) (Bhatt–Scholze Remark 12.11, with the misprint π₁(X) corrected, known issue PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/E20).

π₀ clause (packet-authored, not in Bhatt–Scholze): π₁ of the realisation of the simplicial space X(•) depends only on its 1-skeleton, the bar construction of the commutative monoid π₀X, whose fundamental group is the Grothendieck group of π₀X.
acceptance: For X the discrete Γ-space of an abelian group A, B^n X realises to K(A, n), recovering the Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectrum.
For finite sets, ΩB N(Fin) ≃ ℤ × BΣ_∞⁺ ≃ Ω^∞S^∞.

sources.match: Bhatt–Scholze's statement of Segal's Proposition 1.4.

nodes.title: Segal's group-completion theorem for special Γ-spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be a special Γ-space. Then the natural map |X([1])| → Ω|BX([1])| is a group completion in the sense of H.4/group-completion: it is an H-map for the addition of X, π₀ of the target is the Grothendieck group of the commutative monoid π₀X, and H_*(Ω|BX|; k) ≅ π₀(X)⁻¹ H_*(|X([1])|; k) for every commutative ring k. For X = N(C) (H.4/coherent-subset-construction) this makes BC → Ω|B N(C)| a group completion.
hypotheses: X special; the H-space structure on |X([1])| uses a homotopy inverse of the Segal map and the realisation of products (packet gap 'Realisation of products').
proofSteps: Segal 1974, Proposition 4.1 (for topological monoids McDuff–Segal 1976), quoted by Weibel IV 4.5.1–4.5.2; not read: packet gap 'Group-completion theorem for Segal's machine'.
The π₀ part is the π₀ clause of H.4/segal-delooping-theorem.
acceptance: For X = N(Fin_*) this gives the Barratt–Priddy–Quillen–Segal identification ΩB N ≃ ℤ × BΣ_∞⁺ at the level of homology.
For grouplike X the map is a weak equivalence (H.4/segal-delooping-theorem).

sources.match: The group-completion theorem for topological monoids, cited by Weibel to [Adams].
The same statement for infinite loop space machines applied to symmetric monoidal categories, which is the Γ-space case used here.

uses.how: BC → ΩB N(C) is a group completion
σ₀ is a group completion

nodes.title: Group completion as a left adjoint
nodes.statement: The functor X ↦ X^gp := ΩBX from special Γ-spaces (E∞-monoids) to grouplike ones is left adjoint to the inclusion of grouplike E∞-monoids, (Bhatt–Scholze Corollary 12.12, stated there for ∞-categories without proof; in the strict model: every map from X to a grouplike special Γ-space factors through X → ΩBX up to levelwise weak equivalence, uniquely up to homotopy); the unit X → ΩBX is a group completion in the sense of H.4/group-completion for X = N(C), and for C a symmetric monoidal groupoid with faithful translations whose monoid of isomorphism classes is countable or contains a countable cofinal submonoid (e.g. iso P(R) for any ring R, via the free modules) Ω|B N(C)| and B(C⁻¹C) are weakly homotopy equivalent under BC in the weak-equivalence sense of H.4/group-completion-uniqueness-countable.
hypotheses: Statements at the level of the ∞-categories (or homotopy categories) of E∞-monoids; the comparison with Quillen's S⁻¹S model uses H.4/quillen-localization-of-homology and uniqueness of group completions (H.4/group-completion-uniqueness-countable for countable π₀).
proofSteps: Adjunction: Bhatt–Scholze Corollary 12.12, from Proposition 12.10 (H.4/segal-delooping-theorem); Bhatt–Scholze give no proof, recorded under the gap 'Infinite loop space machine equivalence'.

Comparison with S⁻¹S: both maps BC → ΩB N(C) and BC → B(C⁻¹C) are group completions (homology localisation), hence related by an equivalence for countable π₀ (H.4/group-completion-uniqueness-countable); Weibel 4.5.2 cites May–Thomason for the uniqueness of machines (not read).

The unit BC ≃ |N(C)([1])| → Ω|B N(C)| is a group completion by H.4/segal-group-completion-homology, and the equivalence |N(C)([1])| ≃ BC (coherentSubsetGammaSpace.level_one) carries the Γ-space addition to B(⊗) up to homotopy, so both maps compared are H-maps for compatible H-structures, as H.4/group-completion-uniqueness-countable requires.
acceptance: For C = Pic(R), the unit is an equivalence (C is Picard).
For C = Vect(R), ΩB N(C) ≃ K₀(R) × BGL(R)⁺ by H.4/cofinality-projective-modules.

sources.match: Bhatt–Scholze's group completion as ΩB, left adjoint to the inclusion (Corollary 12.12 follows on the page).

nodes.title: Picard groupoids are exactly the grouplike N(C)
nodes.statement: A symmetric monoidal groupoid C is a Picard groupoid (every object invertible under ⊗) iff the E∞-monoid N(C) is grouplike; then N(C) → ΩB N(C) is an equivalence, and the underlying space Ω|B N(C)| of K(C) is homotopy equivalent to the 1-truncated space |N(C)([1])| ≃ BC (the spectrum-level statement is H.5:spectra/picard-one-truncated-spectra).
hypotheses: C a symmetric monoidal groupoid.
proofSteps: π₀ N(C) is the monoid of isomorphism classes under ⊗ (H.4/coherent-subset-construction), a group iff every object is invertible (Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 12.15 proof).
Grouplike gives N(C) ≃ ΩB N(C) (H.4/segal-delooping-theorem); |N(C)| is 1-truncated (H.1/groupoid-nerve-one-type).
acceptance: Pic(R) and Pic^ℤ(R) are Picard groupoids.
Vect(R) under ⊕ is not Picard (rank is additive and nonnegative).

sources.locator: Appendix §12, Proposition 12.15 and the paragraph after it, pp. 58–59
sources.match: Bhatt–Scholze's Proposition 12.15 and the paragraph after it.

nodes.title: Classical Grothendieck–Witt spaces of the integers as plus constructions
nodes.statement: The classical Grothendieck–Witt spaces GW_cl(ℤ) of the integers are the group completions B(S⁻¹S) of the symmetric monoidal groupoids S of nondegenerate forms over ℤ under orthogonal sum. In each case below every form is an orthogonal summand of one in the stated cofinal sequence, the colimit automorphism group has perfect commutator subgroup, and H.4/cofinal-sequence-plus-comparison identifies the positive (basepoint) component with a plus construction: symmetric forms, π₀ = ℤ ⊕ ℤ (generated by ⟨1⟩, ⟨−1⟩), component B O_{⟨∞,∞⟩}(ℤ)⁺; symplectic forms, π₀ = ℤ, component B Sp_∞(ℤ)⁺; quadratic forms, π₀ = ℤ ⊕ ℤ (H and E₈), component B O_{∞,∞}(ℤ)⁺; (−1)-quadratic forms, π₀ = ℤ ⊕ ℤ/2 (rank and Arf invariant), component B Sp^q_∞(ℤ)⁺.
hypotheses: The classification of forms over ℤ (Serre; Browder for the Arf invariant) and the perfectness of the commutator subgroups are inputs quoted by Calmès et al., not proved here.
proofSteps: Apply H.4/cofinal-sequence-plus-comparison to S with the cofinal sequence n·(⟨1⟩ ⊥ ⟨−1⟩), n·H_s, n·H_q, n·H⁰_{−q} respectively (Calmès et al. §3.2, cases (1)-symmetric, (−1)-symmetric, (1)-quadratic, (−1)-quadratic).
π₀ is the Grothendieck group of isomorphism classes (H.4/S-inverse-S-pi0) computed from the classification theorems quoted there.
acceptance: π₀ GW^q_cl(ℤ) = ℤ ⊕ ℤ with generators H and E₈ (Calmès et al. p. 55).
π₀ GW^{−q}_cl(ℤ) has 2-torsion, from the Arf invariant.

sources.match: Calmès et al. identify each positive component with the plus construction of the infinite automorphism group via the group completion theorem.

nodes.title: Topological variants of functors on rings via simplicial rings
nodes.statement: For a functor F from rings to spaces (or spectra) and a topological ring A (for example ℝ), the topological variant is F^top(A) = |n ↦ F(C(Δⁿ, A))|, the realisation of F applied to the simplicial ring of continuous maps from the topological n-simplex with pointwise operations; there is a natural map F(A) → F^top(A) from the 0-simplices. For F = K, GW, L this gives K^top, GW^top, L^top of ℝ.
hypotheses: F a functor to simplicial sets or spaces (realisations as in H.2/simplicial-space-realisation); A a topological ring.
proofSteps: The simplicial ring n ↦ C(Δⁿ, A) uses Mathlib's topological simplices (SimplexCategory.toTop) and pointwise ring structure; apply F levelwise and realise (Calmès et al. Lemma 3.2.11 proof, following Schlichting §10).
The comparisons K^top(ℝ) ≃ ko, GW^top₀ = GW₀ and the 1-connective cover identifications are quoted from Schlichting 2017 (not read; packet gap 'Topological K-theory of ℝ via simplicial rings').
acceptance: For F constant, F^top(A) = F(A).
K^top(ℝ) ≃ ko, so π₁K^top(ℝ) = ℤ/2 (quoted).

nodes.title: Pointed simplicial sets, smash product and simplicial spheres
nodes.statement: For pointed simplicial sets K, L, the smash product K ∧ L is the quotient (K × L)/(K ∨ L) by the wedge K × {*} ∪ {*} × L; it is symmetric monoidal on pointed simplicial sets with unit S⁰ = Δ[0]₊. The simplicial circle is S¹ = Δ[1]/∂Δ[1] and Sⁿ = (S¹)^{∧n}, with Σ_n acting by permuting the smash factors; |Sⁿ| is homeomorphic to the n-sphere and |K ∧ L| ≅ |K| ∧ |L| when the product is formed in compactly generated spaces. The pointed mapping simplicial set and loop functor Ω K = map_*(S¹, K) are right adjoint to S¹ ∧ −; Ω K has the homotopy type of the loop space of |K| when K is a Kan complex (in general apply it to Ex^∞ K).
hypotheses: Pointed simplicial sets (Under Δ[0] in SSet); realisation of products as in H.1/classifying-space-prod.
proofSteps: Define the wedge and smash as pushouts in SSet (Mathlib has colimits of simplicial sets); associativity, unit and symmetry follow from those of the product.

S¹ = Δ[1]/∂Δ[1] has exactly two nondegenerate simplices (vertex and 1-cell), so |S¹| is a circle (H.1/classifying-space-cw-structure); Sⁿ is the n-fold smash with the coordinate-permuting Σ_n-action used in symmetric spectra (Schwede Definition 3.1, Hovey–Shipley–Smith §1.1).
acceptance: |S¹ ∧ S¹| ≃ S² (two-sphere).
S⁰ ∧ K ≅ K.

nodes.title: Symmetric spectra of simplicial sets
nodes.statement: A symmetric spectrum X consists of pointed simplicial sets X_n (n ≥ 0) with basepoint-preserving left Σ_n-actions and pointed maps σ_n : X_n ∧ S¹ → X_{n+1} such that every iterate σ^m : X_n ∧ S^m → X_{n+m} is Σ_n × Σ_m-equivariant. Morphisms are levelwise equivariant maps commuting with the structure maps; the category Sp of symmetric spectra has all limits and colimits (levelwise). Forgetting the symmetric group actions gives the underlying sequential spectrum. This is the concrete spectrum model of the roadmap, compatible with simplicial sets; geometric realisation levelwise gives symmetric spectra of spaces.
hypotheses: Pointed simplicial sets and simplicial spheres from H.5:spectra/simplicial-spheres-and-smash.
proofSteps: Define the data and the equivariance condition (Schwede Definition 3.1 for simplicial sets; Hovey–Shipley–Smith Definition 1.2.2).
Limits and colimits are formed levelwise with the induced actions and structure maps (Schwede Example 3.5).
acceptance: The sphere spectrum S (Sⁿ in level n) is a symmetric spectrum (Schwede Example 1.8).
The Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectrum HA is one (Schwede Example 1.14; H.5:spectra/eilenberg-maclane-spectrum).

nodes.title: Naive stable homotopy groups indexed by the integers
nodes.statement: For a sequential (or symmetric) spectrum X and k ∈ ℤ, the naive homotopy group π̂_k X = colim_n π_{k+n}|X_n| is the colimit, over n ≥ max(0, 2 − k), of the stabilisation maps π_{k+n}|X_n| → π_{k+n+1}|X_{n+1}| sending f to σ_n ∘ (f ∧ S¹). These are abelian groups, functorial in X, with natural isomorphisms π̂_k(ΩX) ≅ π̂_{k+1}X (for strict simplicial loops assume X levelwise Kan, or take a levelwise Kan replacement) and π̂_k X ≅ π̂_{k+1}(S¹ ∧ X). A π̂_*-isomorphism is a map inducing isomorphisms on all π̂_k.
hypotheses: X a sequential or symmetric spectrum; homotopy groups of realisations (Mathlib HomotopyGroup, Tau Ceti functoriality and loop-space shift).
For Ω computed as strict simplicial mapping spaces, X is levelwise Kan; for the topological loop of the realised spectrum this restriction is unnecessary (Schwede I Proposition 3.8, p. 37).
proofSteps: Define the stabilisation maps through suspension of representing maps and take the filtered colimit of abelian groups (Schwede Definition 2.1).
Loop and suspension isomorphisms are compatible with stabilisation, giving the shifts (Schwede (2.3)–(2.4) and Proposition 2.6), using Tau Ceti's HomotopyGroup.pathLoopSpaceMulEquiv.
acceptance: π̂_k S = π^s_k, the stable stems; π̂_k S = 0 for k < 0.
π̂_* HA = A in degree 0 (H.5:spectra/eilenberg-maclane-spectrum).

nodes.title: Ω-spectra and connective spectra
nodes.statement: A symmetric spectrum X is an Ω-spectrum if every adjoint structure map σ̃_n : |X_n| → Ω|X_{n+1}| is a weak homotopy equivalence (each X_n Kan, or after realisation); then π̂_k X ≅ π_{k+n}|X_n| for k + n ≥ 0, and π̂_k X = π₀|X_{−k}| for k < 0. X is naively connective if π̂_k X = 0 for k < 0; this implies connectivity in the sense of true homotopy groups (H.5:spectra/true-homotopy-groups; Schwede I Example 8.50) but not conversely. Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectra (H.5:spectra/eilenberg-maclane-spectrum) are Ω-spectra. The unreplaced S-construction spectrum is only a positive Ω-spectrum: its zeroth level |wC| need not be equivalent to Ω|wS.C|. Taking Ω|wS.C| as zeroth space and compatible fibrant replacements gives its connective Ω-spectrum model. Negative homotopy groups depend on the chosen deloopings, not on the zeroth space.
hypotheses: Kan levels (or realisation) so that Ω is the homotopically correct loop space.
proofSteps: Define IsOmegaSpectrum through H.2/weak-homotopy-equivalence of the adjoint structure maps (Schwede Definition 1.15).
For an Ω-spectrum the colimit defining π̂_k stabilises at the first defined stage (loop-space shift).
acceptance: π_n of the Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectrum of A is A in degree 0 and zero otherwise.
Weibel IV 8.5.5: the S.-construction gives a connective Ω-spectrum with π_i = K_i for i ≥ 0.
Negative homotopy groups of a spectrum depend on the chosen deloopings (Weibel IV §2 remark on K_m(R; Z/ℓ) for m < 2).

nodes.title: Suspension spectra, free spectra and the sphere spectrum
nodes.statement: For a pointed simplicial set K, the suspension spectrum Σ^∞K has levels K ∧ Sⁿ with Σ_n permuting the sphere coordinates and structure maps the canonical isomorphisms; Σ^∞ is left adjoint to evaluation at level 0. The sphere spectrum is S = Σ^∞S⁰. More generally the free spectrum F_m K (left adjoint to evaluation at level m) is trivial below level m and has (F_m K)_{m+n} = Σ_{m+n,+} ∧_{1×Σ_n} K ∧ Sⁿ, where 1 × Σ_n fixes the first m letters (Schwede I Example 3.20). Σ^∞_+ X := Σ^∞(X₊).
hypotheses: K a pointed simplicial set.
proofSteps: Define levels and structure maps (Schwede Example 1.13 for spaces; Example 3.20 for free spectra).
The adjunction Σ^∞ ⊣ ev₀ and F_m ⊣ ev_m are checked levelwise from the universal property of the free Σ_n-object.
acceptance: π̂_k Σ^∞K = π^s_k(K), the stable homotopy groups of K; Σ^∞K is connective.
F₁S¹ is stably equivalent to S but not π̂_*-isomorphic to it (Schwede §I.6).

nodes.title: Loop, suspension and shift of spectra
nodes.statement: For a symmetric spectrum X: the loop spectrum ΩX has levels map_*(S¹, X_n) (homotopically correct when X is levelwise Kan; in general apply it to a levelwise Kan replacement) and the suspension S¹ ∧ X has levels S¹ ∧ X_n, adjoint to each other; the shift sh X has (sh X)_n = X_{1+n} with Σ_n acting through Σ_n → Σ_{1+n}; λ_X : S¹ ∧ X → sh X has components λ_n = χ_{n,1} ∘ σ_n ∘ twist (Schwede I (3.12)). The loop and suspension maps shift naive homotopy groups by one (H.5:spectra/naive-homotopy-groups).
hypotheses: Symmetric spectra; Ω is the strict simplicial loop functor, homotopically correct on levelwise Kan spectra (Schwede I Prop. 3.8).
proofSteps: Define ΩX, S¹ ∧ X and the adjunction levelwise (Schwede §2.1); define sh X and λ_X (Schwede Example 3.9).

For topological loops, π̂_k(ΩX) ≅ π̂_{k+1}X and π̂_k X ≅ π̂_{k+1}(S¹ ∧ X) (Schwede I Proposition 2.6). For strict simplicial loops, use the levelwise Kan hypothesis to compare their realisation with topological loops (Proposition 3.8).
acceptance: Ω and S¹ ∧ − are mutually inverse up to stable equivalence (Schwede II Proposition 2.2).
π̂_{k+1}(sh X) = π̂_k X (Schwede I Example 3.9).

nodes.title: The naive homotopy long exact sequence of a mapping cone
nodes.statement: For every map f : X → Y of symmetric spectra, the sequence ⋯ → π̂_k X → π̂_k Y → π̂_k C(f) →δ π̂_{k−1} X → ⋯ is exact in every integer degree, naturally in commutative squares. The boundary is induced by C(f) → S¹∧X and the inverse suspension isomorphism; no stable replacement or true homotopy group is used.
hypotheses: No semistability hypothesis. Forget symmetric actions to the underlying sequential spectrum; mapping cones and naive groups use the same level constructions.
proofSteps: Use the levelwise cone null-homotopy for image ⊆ kernel at π̂_kY. A representative in the kernel is made null after sufficiently many structure maps; its stable null-homotopy gives a representative from π̂_kX (Schwede I Proposition 2.12).

Apply the same argument to the cone inclusion Y → C(f). The double-cone comparison with S¹∧X and the suspension isomorphism transport exactness to the remaining two terms, with the minus sign from the interval reflection (Schwede I (2.11) and proof of Proposition 2.12). These are cone and suspension arguments independent of true groups.
acceptance: For f = id, the sequence has trivial cone groups.
For X → 0, δ identifies π̂_k C(f) with π̂_{k−1}X.

sources.locator: Chapter I, (2.11), Proposition 2.12 and proof, printed pp. 26–28 (PDF 27–29)
sources.match: The mapping-cone exact sequence is proved for naive groups before semistability and true groups; forgetting actions preserves the construction.

uses.how: A naive isomorphism has a mapping cone with zero naive groups, without using true-group exactness.

nodes.title: The naive homotopy long exact sequence of a homotopy fibre
nodes.statement: For every map f : X → Y of symmetric spectra, with the levelwise homotopy fibre formed after functorial Kan replacement, ⋯ → π̂_k F(f) → π̂_k X → π̂_k Y →δ π̂_{k−1}F(f) → ⋯ is exact in all integer degrees, naturally in commutative squares. The boundary is ΩY → F(f) composed with the inverse naive loop isomorphism.
hypotheses: For the strict simplicial fibre model use Kan levels of X and Y; otherwise replace levels functorially. Level equivalences preserve naive groups.
proofSteps: Apply H.2/long-exact-sequence in each realised level, compatibly with the spectrum structure maps and the chosen interval orientation. In any fixed stable degree the groups are eventually abelian.

Take the filtered colimit of the level sequences. Exactness of filtered colimits in ModuleCat (instAB5ModuleCat with R = ℤ) gives exactness in every stable degree. Identify the boundary using the naive loop isomorphism (Schwede I (2.15) and Proposition 2.17).
acceptance: For 0 → Y the fibre groups equal π̂_{k+1}Y.
For id_X the fibre groups vanish.

nodes.title: Semistable symmetric spectra
nodes.statement: A symmetric spectrum X is semistable if λ_X : S¹ ∧ X → sh X is a π̂_*-isomorphism. Semistability is invariant under π̂_*-isomorphisms and closed under wedges, finite products, S¹ ∧ −, sh and mapping cones (Schwede I Props. 3.15–3.16); Ω-spectra are semistable (for X levelwise Kan, λ̃_X : X → Ω sh X is levelwise σ̃_n followed by the permutation χ_{n,1}, hence a level equivalence; Prop. 3.15(iii)); suspension spectra are semistable (Prop. 3.16(vi)). The comparison of naive and true groups is in H.5:spectra/true-homotopy-groups; Eilenberg–Mac Lane and K-theory spectra are treated in their own nodes.
hypotheses: X a symmetric spectrum of simplicial sets.
proofSteps: Define via λ_X (Schwede Definition 3.14); closure properties (realisation, π̂_*-isomorphism invariance, wedges) are Schwede Propositions 3.15–3.16.
Ω-spectra: λ̃_X is a level equivalence for levelwise Kan Ω-spectra (Prop. 3.15(iii)); suspension spectra: even permutations act trivially on homotopy groups of the levels (Prop. 3.16(vi)).
acceptance: The sphere spectrum is semistable; F₁S¹ is not.
A spectrum whose underlying sequential spectrum is an Ω-spectrum from some level on is semistable.

nodes.title: Stable equivalences of symmetric spectra
nodes.statement: A morphism f : X → Y of symmetric spectra is a stable equivalence if for every injective Ω-spectrum E the induced map [Y, E] → [X, E] on homotopy classes of maps (homotopies X ∧ Δ[1]₊ → E) is bijective (Hovey–Shipley–Smith Definition 3.1.3; Schwede I Definition 4.11). Level equivalences are stable equivalences and stable equivalences satisfy two-out-of-three. That π̂_*-isomorphisms are stable equivalences is H.5:spectra/naive-isomorphism-is-stable-equivalence; the characterisation by true homotopy groups is in H.5:spectra/true-homotopy-groups.
hypotheses: Injective Ω-spectra: Ω-spectra with the right lifting property against levelwise cofibrations that are levelwise weak equivalences.
proofSteps: Definition via injective Ω-spectra (Hovey–Shipley–Smith Definition 3.1.3).
Level equivalences are stable equivalences because a level equivalence between injective spectra is a homotopy equivalence (Schwede I Prop. 4.6 and p. 65).
acceptance: S ∧ X → X is a stable equivalence for every X.

nodes.title: π̂_*-isomorphisms are stable equivalences
nodes.statement: Every π̂_*-isomorphism f : X → Y of symmetric spectra of simplicial sets is a stable equivalence (Hovey–Shipley–Smith Definition 3.1.3).
hypotheses: X, Y symmetric spectra of simplicial sets; levelwise Kan replacement is level-equivalent, hence harmless.
proofSteps: For an injective Ω-spectrum E, λ^∞_E : E → Ω^∞sh^∞E (mapping telescope of ΩⁿshⁿE) is a level equivalence, so it has a homotopy retraction r (Schwede I Prop. 4.19 and Prop. 4.6).

If C is levelwise Kan with π̂_*C = 0 then Ω^∞sh^∞C is levelwise weakly contractible (its unstable groups are π̂_{l−n}(ΩⁿshⁿC) = 0, Schwede I Prop. 4.20), so [C, E] is a point for every injective Ω-spectrum E.

Apply this to the mapping cone of a π̂_*-isomorphism (long exact sequence, H.5:spectra/naive-cofibre-long-exact-sequence) and conclude with the cofibre sequence of [−, E] (Schwede I proof of Thm. 4.23).
acceptance: F₁S¹ → S is a stable equivalence although not a π̂_*-isomorphism, so the converse fails.
A level equivalence is a π̂_*-isomorphism, hence a stable equivalence.

nodes.title: True homotopy groups of symmetric spectra
nodes.statement: For a symmetric spectrum X and k ∈ ℤ, the true homotopy group π_k X is the naive homotopy group π̂_k(QX) of a functorial stable equivalence X → QX to an Ω-spectrum (Schwede I Def. 6.1); a morphism is a stable equivalence iff it induces isomorphisms of all π_k (Schwede I Thm. 6.2). X is connective if π_k X = 0 for k < 0. Representability by spheres in SHC is in H.5:spectra/stable-homotopy-category. There is a natural map π̂_k X → π_k X, an isomorphism for semistable X.
hypotheses: A functorial stable equivalence X → QX to an Ω-spectrum, e.g. the fibrant replacement of the projective stable model structure (H.5:spectra/stable-model-structure).
proofSteps: Define π_k X := π̂_k(QX) (Schwede Definition 6.1); naturality from functoriality of Q.
π̂_*-isomorphisms induce isomorphisms of true groups and f is a stable equivalence iff all π_k f are bijective (Schwede I Thm. 6.2); for semistable X the map π̂_k X → π_k X is bijective (Prop. 6.3).
acceptance: π_k S = π^s_k.
π_*(F₁S¹) = π^s_* although π̂_*(F₁S¹) is larger.

nodes.title: The smash pairing of true homotopy groups
nodes.statement: There is a unique family of natural biadditive pairings · : π_k X × π_l Y → π_{k+l}(X ∧ Y), k, l ∈ ℤ, with 1 · 1 = 1 in π₀S and (a₁)_*((S¹ ∧ x) · y) = S¹ ∧ (x · y) = (−1)^k (a₂)_*(x · (S¹ ∧ y)); it is unital, associative and graded commutative: (τ_{X,Y})_*(x · y) = (−1)^{kl} y · x.
hypotheses: True homotopy groups; the point-set smash product (for the derived product see H.5:spectra/homotopy-group-pairing).
proofSteps: For fixed y ∈ π_l Y, stable natural transformations π_k → π_{k+l}(− ∧ Y) are determined by their value on 1 ∈ π₀S (Schwede I Prop. 6.5, Cor. 6.14); define x · y as the value of the one sending 1 to y.
Commutativity and associativity follow from uniqueness, the sign (−1)^{kl} from the degree of the shuffle χ_{k,l} of spheres (Schwede I Lemma 1.10, Thm. 6.16).

nodes.title: The stable model structure on symmetric spectra
nodes.statement: The category of symmetric spectra of simplicial sets admits a (cofibrantly generated, simplicial) model structure whose weak equivalences are the stable equivalences, whose cofibrations are the projective cofibrations, and whose fibrant objects are the Ω-spectra with Kan levels; there is also the positive projective (and flat) stable model structure with the same weak equivalences. Functorial factorisations (from the small object argument, Mathlib's MorphismProperty.FunctorialFactorizationData; Mathlib's ModelCategory itself only asserts existence) give functorial cofibrant and fibrant replacements. Its homotopy category is the stable homotopy category.
hypotheses: Mathlib's HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory; the Kan–Quillen model structure on simplicial sets is used levelwise (not in Mathlib; recorded as the packet gap 'Kan–Quillen model structure').
proofSteps: Hovey–Shipley–Smith Theorem 3.4.4 (factorisations Cor. 3.4.6 and Lemma 3.4.8, lifting Cor. 3.4.7) from the projective level model structure (HSS Thm. 5.1.2); Schwede III Thm. 4.11 gives the positive and flat variants (its proof is incomplete in v3.0).
Fibrant objects are Ω-spectra with Kan levels (Hovey–Shipley–Smith §3.4).
acceptance: Cofibrant replacement of S is S itself.
The stable model structure is stable: suspension is invertible on the homotopy category.

nodes.title: The stable homotopy category
nodes.statement: The stable homotopy category SHC is the localisation γ : Sp → SHC of symmetric spectra at the stable equivalences (a localisation functor in the sense of Mathlib's Functor.IsLocalization, hence equivalent to MorphismProperty.Localization, whose hom-types lie in a larger universe), with hom-sets [X, Y] = homotopy classes of maps from X to a chosen injective Ω-spectrum replacement of Y; a morphism of spectra is a stable equivalence iff γ of it is an isomorphism. SHC is additive (finite sums and products agree), the suspension Σ = S¹ ∧ − is an autoequivalence, and π_k X = [S^k, X].
hypotheses: Choices of injective Ω-spectrum replacements; any two choices give canonically isomorphic categories.
proofSteps: Define SHC with morphisms [X, ωY] for a functorial stable equivalence p_Y : Y → ωY to an injective Ω-spectrum (Schwede I Props. 4.10, 4.39; HSS Cor. 5.1.3) (Schwede II Definition 1.1) and prove the localisation property (Theorem 1.6), matching Mathlib's MorphismProperty.Localization through its universal property.
Additivity: finite coproducts and products agree (Schwede II Proposition 1.10, Corollary 1.13; H.5:spectra/finite-biproducts).
Σ is an equivalence (Schwede II Proposition 2.2).

π_k X ≅ SHC(S^k, X) by evaluation at the fundamental class (Schwede II Example 1.15); SHC(Σ^∞K, X) ≅ [K, X₀] for Ω-spectra X with Kan levels (Example 1.17); π_* detects isomorphisms (Prop. 1.9), used for additivity (Cor. 1.13).
acceptance: The functor γ sends F₁S¹ → S to an isomorphism.
SHC(S, HA) = A.

nodes.title: Mapping cones and homotopy fibres of spectra
nodes.statement: For a morphism f : X → Y of symmetric spectra, the mapping cone C(f) = Y ∪_f (Δ[1] ∧ X) (with Δ[1] pointed at the vertex 0 and X ⊂ Δ[1] ∧ X along the vertex 1, as in Schwede I (2.8) and II Example 2.4; the projection Y ∪_f (Δ[1] ∧ X) → S¹ ∧ X collapses Y and maps Δ[1] → Δ[1]/∂Δ[1] = S¹) and the homotopy fibre F(f) = X ×_Y Y^{Δ[1]} (levelwise on Kan replacements) come with natural maps Y → C(f) → S¹ ∧ X and ΩY → F(f) → X. They are functorial in commutative squares; their invariance under stable equivalences is in H.5:spectra/cofibre-long-exact-sequence.
hypotheses: Symmetric spectra; homotopy fibres after levelwise Kan replacement.
proofSteps: Levelwise mapping cones and homotopy fibres with induced actions and structure maps (Schwede II Examples 2.4, 2.6; Schwede I §2 for sequential spectra).
acceptance: C(id_X) is contractible (stably trivial).

nodes.title: Long exact sequences of homotopy groups for cofibres and fibres of spectra
nodes.statement: For every morphism f : X → Y of symmetric spectra, the sequences ⋯ → π_k X → π_k Y → π_k C(f) →δ π_{k−1} X → ⋯ and ⋯ → π_k F(f) → π_k X → π_k Y → π_{k−1} F(f) → ⋯ of abelian groups are exact in all integer degrees, naturally in f, for true homotopy groups; the two naive sequences are separate earlier inputs. Consequently a map of arrows whose components are stable equivalences induces stable equivalences of mapping cones and homotopy fibres (five lemma and Schwede I Thm. 6.2).
hypotheses: Every map of symmetric spectra; the homotopy fibre uses functorial levelwise Kan replacements. The true-group comparison uses stable Ω-replacements.
proofSteps: True homotopy groups: Schwede I Prop. 6.11 (fibre sequence for levelwise Kan X, Y; F(f) is formed on levelwise Kan replacements), using that mapping cones of morphisms between semistable spectra are semistable (Prop. 3.16(v)).
acceptance: For m : S → S, the cofibre sequence gives π_k S/m (H.6/bockstein-long-exact-sequence).
Unlike for spaces, all terms are abelian groups and the sequence continues in negative degrees.

sources.match: Schwede's long exact sequence for the mapping cone; Proposition 2.17 (p. 29) gives the fibre version.
The true-homotopy version, with the levelwise Kan hypothesis for fibres.

nodes.title: Fibre and cofibre sequences agree up to a shift
nodes.statement: For f : X → Y, the natural map h : S¹ ∧ F(f) → C(f) of Schwede I (2.16) is a π̂_*-isomorphism, hence a stable equivalence, and so is its adjoint F(f) → ΩC(f) when C(f) is levelwise Kan. Under h_* ∘ (S¹ ∧ −) the connecting maps of the two long exact sequences correspond up to the sign −1: h_*(S¹ ∧ δ_F(y)) = −i_*(y) for y ∈ π̂_{1+k}Y (Schwede I proof of Prop. 2.17).
hypotheses: Symmetric spectra.
proofSteps: h is a π̂_*-isomorphism by comparing the fibre and cofibre long exact sequences with the five lemma (Schwede I Prop. 2.17), hence a stable equivalence (H.5:spectra/naive-isomorphism-is-stable-equivalence); its adjoint F(f) → ΩC(f) is one for levelwise Kan C(f) (Prop. 3.8).
acceptance: F(X → 0) = X and ΩC(X → 0) = ΩΣX ≃ X.
This stability fails for spaces: the fibre of S¹ → point is S¹, not Ω of its cofibre.

sources.match: Schwede's comparison of fibre and cofibre; the stable equivalence follows.

nodes.title: Finite wedges and products of spectra agree
nodes.statement: For symmetric spectra X, Y the canonical map X ∨ Y → X × Y is a π̂_*-isomorphism (hence a stable equivalence), and π̂_k of an arbitrary wedge is the sum, π̂_k of a finite product the product, of the π̂_k.
hypotheses: Finite products for the product statement; arbitrary wedges for the sum statement.
proofSteps: Schwede I Prop. 2.19: for a wedge A ∨ B the inclusion of A has a retraction, so the long exact sequence of Prop. 2.12 splits; finite products are levelwise; the wedge-to-product map is a π̂_*-isomorphism by (i) and (ii), hence a stable equivalence (H.5:spectra/naive-isomorphism-is-stable-equivalence).
acceptance: S ∨ S → S × S is a stable equivalence but not a levelwise weak equivalence (level 1: S¹ ∨ S¹ → S¹ × S¹).

sources.match: Schwede's Proposition 2.19 (wedges and finite products); additivity is II Corollary 1.13.

nodes.title: Products in the stable homotopy category
nodes.statement: The stable homotopy category has products of arbitrary families: if ω(Y^i) are injective Ω-spectrum replacements of symmetric spectra Y^i, the point-set product ∏_i ω(Y^i) with its projections is a product of the Y^i in SHC; γ preserves finite products. Consequently π_k(∏_i Y^i) ≅ ∏_i π_k(Y^i) for all k ∈ ℤ, since π_k = SHC(S^k, −).
hypotheses: Arbitrary index sets; the point-set product of the Y^i themselves is in general not a product in SHC (Schwede I Example 4.33).
proofSteps: A product of injective Ω-spectra is an injective Ω-spectrum, and SHC(X, Z) = [X, Z] for Z an injective Ω-spectrum (H.5:spectra/stable-homotopy-category), so SHC(X, ∏ω(Y^i)) = ∏ SHC(X, Y^i) (Schwede II Proposition 1.10(ii) and its proof).
π_k commutes with products because it is represented by S^k (H.5:spectra/true-homotopy-groups).
acceptance: The countable products used by H.6/homotopy-limit-of-tower and ∏_p X^∧_p in H.6/arithmetic-fracture-square exist.

sources.locator: Chapter II, Proposition 1.10(ii) and proof, pp. 220–221 (PDF 221–222)
sources.match: Existence of products in SHC via products of injective Ω-spectra.

nodes.title: The smash product of symmetric spectra
nodes.statement: The smash product X ∧ Y of symmetric spectra is the universal recipient of a bimorphism, i.e. of Σ_p × Σ_q-equivariant maps X_p ∧ Y_q → (X ∧ Y)_{p+q} compatible with the structure maps; concretely (X ∧ Y)_n = ⋁_{p+q=n} Σ_{n+} ∧_{Σ_p × Σ_q} X_p ∧ Y_q modulo the relations from the structure maps. With the associativity isomorphism and the twist isomorphism (which involves the shuffle permutation χ_{q,p}), ∧ is a closed symmetric monoidal structure on symmetric spectra with strict unit S and internal function spectra Hom(Y, Z).
hypotheses: Symmetric spectra of simplicial sets; the closed structure uses the internal Hom spectrum.
proofSteps: Construct X ∧ Y as a coequaliser realising the universal bimorphism (Schwede I Construction 5.6).
Associativity, symmetry with the shuffle χ_{q,p}, unit S and the adjunction with Hom (Schwede I Theorem 5.10; Hovey–Shipley–Smith §2.2).
acceptance: S ∧ X ≅ X.

nodes.title: The sign of the twist on spheres
nodes.statement: For m, n ∈ ℤ let α_{m,n} : S^{m+n} → S^m ∧^L S^n be the morphism of SHC with (α_{m,n})_*(ι_{m+n}) = ι_m · ι_n (Schwede II (4.3)). Each α_{m,n} is an isomorphism; α_{m,0} and α_{0,n} are identities; α is associative; and the twist satisfies τ̄_{S^m,S^n} ∘ α_{m,n} = α_{n,m} ∘ (−1)^{mn}.
hypotheses: Spheres S^n = Σ^n S (n ≥ 0) and F_{−n}S⁰ (n < 0) with fundamental classes ι_n ∈ π_n S^n; · is the pairing of H.5:spectra/true-homotopy-pairing.
proofSteps: Sphere representability (Schwede II Example 1.15) reduces the associativity and commutativity squares to the associativity and the sign (−1)^{kl} of the pairing of true homotopy groups (Schwede I Thm. 6.16); α_{1,n} agrees with β_n of II (4.2), so it is an isomorphism, and induction on |m| gives invertibility of all α_{m,n} (Schwede II Prop. 4.4).
acceptance: For m even (any n), α_{n,m}^{−1} ∘ τ̄_{S^m,S^n} ∘ α_{m,n} is the identity of S^{m+n}.
For m = −1, n = 1 the twist on S^{−1} ∧^L S^1 ≅ S^0 is −1.

nodes.title: The smash pairing on homotopy groups
nodes.statement: For symmetric spectra X, Y there is a natural biadditive pairing · : π_p X ⊗ π_q Y → π_{p+q}(X ∧^L Y), x · y = (x ∧ y) ∘ α_{p,q}, associative and unital (with 1 ∈ π₀ S), graded commutative in the sense that τ_*(x · y) = (−1)^{pq} y · x, and compatible with maps: (f ∧ f′)_*(y · y′) = (−1)^{m′n} f_*(y) · f′_*(y′) for f of degree m, f′ of degree m′ and y ∈ π_n.
hypotheses: True homotopy groups; derived smash product.
proofSteps: Define the pairing by smashing representatives and composing with α_{p,q} of H.5:spectra/twist-sign (Schwede II §4, (4.13)); the action of π^s_* on π_* X is the case Y = S (Schwede I Example 1.11).
Sign rules: Schwede II Proposition 4.11 with H.5:spectra/twist-sign.
acceptance: π_*S = π^s_* is a graded-commutative ring under this pairing (η² ≠ 0 in π₂).

nodes.title: Stable model structures on module spectra
nodes.statement: For a symmetric ring spectrum R, the category of right R-modules has a cofibrantly generated, proper, simplicial stable model structure (absolute projective; also positive projective and flat variants) whose weak equivalences and fibrations are those of the underlying symmetric spectra; it is monoidal for ∧_R when R is commutative. Its homotopy category Ho(R-Mod) is triangulated, with distinguished triangles the cone triangles of R-modules, and the free–forgetful adjunction gives Ho(R-Mod)(X ∧ᴸ R, M) ≅ SHC(X, M).
hypotheses: Packet gap: the transfer along the free functor needs the monoid axiom for the stable model structure (Schwede IV §1, proofs not decomposed).
proofSteps: Transfer the stable model structure along − ∧ R ⊣ forget (Schwede IV Thm. 1.3), using the monoid axiom.
Stability and the triangulated structure follow as for spectra, since the forgetful functor preserves cones and S¹ ∧ −.
acceptance: R = S gives the stable model structure of symmetric spectra.
For R = HZ, Ho(HZ-Mod) ≃ D(ℤ) (H.5:spectra/eilenberg-maclane-of-chain-complex).

nodes.title: Operads and E∞-algebras in symmetric spectra
nodes.statement: An operad O of symmetric spectra is a sequence O(n) with right Σ_n-actions, a unit S → O(1) and associative, equivariant, unital composition maps; an O-algebra is a spectrum A with maps O(n) ∧_{Σ_n} A^{∧n} → A. Equivariance: γ is compatible with the right actions on the O(i_j), the block-sum action on O(i₁ + ⋯ + i_n) and the permutation of blocks by Σ_n (the conditions left blank in Schwede III Defs. 5.3–5.4). For an E∞ operad of simplicial sets (contractible O(n) with free Σ_n-action), O-algebras realise E∞-ring spectra; commutative symmetric ring spectra are Com-algebras. Algebras over suitable operads carry model structures with weak equivalences the underlying stable equivalences, and E∞-algebras and commutative symmetric ring spectra have equivalent homotopy theories (in the positive model structure). The comparison with the abstract E∞-algebras of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract is part of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:spectra-comparison.
hypotheses: Positive (flat) stable model structure for model structures on algebras; the E∞/commutative comparison is quoted (Schwede III §6), not proved in the passages read (packet gap 'Model structures on algebras over operads').
proofSteps: Define operads and algebras (Schwede III Definitions 5.3, 5.4); operads of simplicial sets give operads of spectra by Σ^∞₊ (Example 5.6).
Model structures on O-algebras: Schwede III §6 (quoted).
acceptance: Com-algebras are commutative symmetric ring spectra; Ass-algebras are ring spectra (Schwede III Examples 5.9–5.10).
HR for commutative R is a Com-algebra.

nodes.title: Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectra of abelian groups
nodes.statement: For an abelian group A, the Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectrum HA has n-th level the reduced A-linearisation A[Sⁿ] (the simplicial abelian group A ⊗ ℤ̃[Sⁿ]), with Σ_n permuting sphere coordinates and structure maps (Σ a_i x_i) ∧ y ↦ Σ a_i (x_i ∧ y). Each |A[Sⁿ]| is a K(A, n) (Dold–Thom), HA is an Ω-spectrum with π₀ HA = A and π_k HA = 0 for k ≠ 0, and A ↦ HA is a functor Ab → Sp with H(A ⊕ B) ≅ HA × HB levelwise. For the integers, HZ = (ℤ̃[Sⁿ]) as in Hovey–Shipley–Smith Example 1.2.5.
hypotheses: A abelian. The identification |A[Sⁿ]| ≃ K(A, n) uses the Dold–Kan correspondence (Mathlib) and the computation of homotopy groups of simplicial abelian groups as homology of their normalised complexes (Moore), not in the libraries (packet gap 'Homotopy groups of simplicial abelian groups').
proofSteps: Define the levels and structure maps (Schwede I Example 1.14; Hovey–Shipley–Smith Example 1.2.5).

π_k |A[Sⁿ]| = H̃_k(Sⁿ; A), via the normalised chains of A[Sⁿ] (Mathlib's Dold–Kan normalised Moore complex) and Moore's theorem; hence A[Sⁿ] is a K(A, n) (H.3/eilenberg-maclane-space) and σ̃_n is a weak equivalence (Schwede I p. 17).
Hence HA is an Ω-spectrum with naive (= true) homotopy concentrated in degree 0 (Schwede I after Definition 1.15).
acceptance: H(ℤ/2) has π₀ = ℤ/2.
H is additive: H(A ⊕ B) ≅ HA × HB ≃ HA ∨ HB.

sources.match: Schwede's construction; p. 17 shows HA is an Ω-spectrum with π̂₀ HA = A.

nodes.title: Maps into Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectra and their uniqueness
nodes.statement: (i) For a coconnective X (π_k X = 0 for k ≥ 1) and a connective A, π₀ : SHC(A, X) → Hom(π₀A, π₀X) is an isomorphism; in particular SHC(A, HB) ≅ Hom(π₀A, B). (ii) If π_k X = 0 for k ≠ 0, there is a unique morphism H(π₀X) → X in SHC inducing the identity on π₀, and it is an isomorphism. (iii) π₀ is an equivalence from the full subcategory of SHC of spectra with homotopy concentrated in degree 0 to abelian groups.
hypotheses: True homotopy groups; HA from H.5:spectra/eilenberg-maclane-spectrum.
proofSteps: (i) by induction over ⟨S⟩⁺ (H.5:spectra/connective-generation), starting from SHC(S, X) ≅ π₀X (Schwede II Prop. 5.24).
(ii) and (iii) follow from (i) applied to HA, which is coconnective (Schwede II Thm. 5.25).

SHC(S, HA) ≅ A.

nodes.title: HR as a ring spectrum and HR-modules
nodes.statement: For a ring R, HR is a symmetric ring spectrum with multiplication R[S^p] ∧ R[S^q] → R[S^{p+q}], (Σ a_i x_i) ∧ (Σ b_j y_j) ↦ Σ a_i b_j (x_i ∧ y_j), commutative when R is; a right R-module M makes HM a right HR-module spectrum, via M[S^p]∧R[S^q] → M[S^{p+q}], (Σ m_i x_i)∧(Σ r_j y_j) ↦ Σ (m_i r_j)(x_i∧y_j).
hypotheses: R a ring (commutative for the commutative ring spectrum and for Shipley's comparison).

Module spectra in this packet are right modules; for a noncommutative R the input right R-module is encoded in Lean by Module Rᵐᵒᵖ M. For commutative R the left/right convention agrees through the canonical conversion.
proofSteps: The multiplication is the linearisation of the smash of spheres (Schwede I Example 1.14 and §1; Hovey–Shipley–Smith).

An HR-module with homotopy concentrated in degree 0 is stably equivalent, as an HR-module, to H(π₀M).

nodes.title: The Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectrum of a chain complex
nodes.statement: There is a functor H : Ch(ℤ) → HZ-Mod from unbounded chain complexes of abelian groups (Shipley's derived composite U ∘ L ∘ c ∘ R), sending quasi-isomorphisms to stable equivalences and inducing an equivalence D(ℤ) ≃ Ho(HZ-Mod) with ℤ[0] ↦ HZ; for a commutative ring R the same construction gives Ho(HR-Mod) ≃ D(R). Conventions: a chain complex C is the Mathlib cochain complex with C^n = C_{−n}, and C[1] denotes C⟦1⟧, (C⟦1⟧)^n = C^{n+1}, i.e. C[1]_n = C_{n−1}. Homotopy groups, shifts and H(A[0]) ≃ HA are in H.5:spectra/eilenberg-maclane-of-chain-complex-homotopy.
hypotheses: Unbounded chain complexes of abelian groups (or R-modules); the derived functor H = U L^{mon} c R of Shipley.
proofSteps: Define H as the composite U ∘ L ∘ c ∘ R of Shipley's zig-zag through Sp^Σ(sAb) and Sp^Σ(ch₊) (Shipley §2.2), where the Sp^Σ(sAb) → Sp^Σ(ch₊) step φ*N applies Mathlib's Dold–Kan normalisation levelwise together with the lax symmetric monoidal (Eilenberg–Zilber shuffle) structure of N and the ring map φ : Sym(ℤ[1]) → N(ℤ̃S), neither of which Mathlib provides at the pin; its left adjoint L is not the levelwise Dold–Kan inverse.

The three adjunctions are Quillen equivalences whose right adjoints preserve all weak equivalences (Shipley Prop. 2.10, proved in Shipley §§3–4 from [SS03b]; packet gap 'Shipley's zig-zag of monoidal Quillen equivalences'), so quasi-isomorphisms go to stable equivalences and D(ℤ) ≃ Ho(HZ-Mod); ℤ may be replaced by any commutative ring (Shipley p. 5).
acceptance: For m ≠ 0 and C = (ℤ →·m ℤ) in homological degrees 1, 0, H(C) ≃ H(ℤ/m).
π_k H(C) for C with H_* = ℤ in degrees 0 and −1 has π₀ = ℤ and π_{−1} = ℤ.

nodes.title: Homotopy groups of the Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectrum of a chain complex
nodes.statement: For every unbounded complex C of abelian groups (Mathlib cochain complex, C^n = C_{−n}) there are natural isomorphisms π_k(HC) ≅ H_k(C) = H^{−k}(C) for all k ∈ ℤ; H(C⟦1⟧) ≅ ΣHC naturally (so H_k(C⟦1⟧) = H_{k−1}(C)), H sends distinguished triangles of D(ℤ) to distinguished triangles of SHC, and H(A[0]) ≃ HA naturally in A.
hypotheses: H from H.5:spectra/eilenberg-maclane-of-chain-complex; Mathlib's shift and mapping-cone conventions on cochain complexes.
proofSteps: The Quillen equivalences give an exact equivalence D(ℤ) ≃ Ho(HZ-Mod) sending ℤ[0] to HZ; π_k(HC) = SHC(S^k, HC) ≅ Ho(HZ-Mod)(Σ^k HZ, HC) ≅ D(ℤ)(ℤ placed in cochain degree −k, C) = H^{−k}(C) (free–forgetful adjunction of H.5:spectra/module-spectra-model-structure; exactness: the triangulation induced by the stable model structure on Ho(Ch(ℤ)) agrees with Mathlib's shift and cone sign on DerivedCategory ℤ (packet gap 'Shipley's zig-zag of monoidal Quillen equivalences'; the dg-nerve analogue is EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E0/stable-api-and-the-sign-comparison)).
H(A[0]) has homotopy A in degree 0, so it is HA by H.5:spectra/eilenberg-maclane-uniqueness.

nodes.title: Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectra represent ordinary cohomology
nodes.statement: For a pointed simplicial set (or CW complex) K, an abelian group A and k ≥ 0, the natural map H̃^k(K; A) → [Σ^∞K, Σ^k HA]_{SHC} = H^k(Σ^∞K; A) is an isomorphism, and the right side vanishes for k < 0; unpointed: [Σ^∞_+X, Σ^k HA] ≅ H^k(X; A) (singular cohomology, Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology stage 6). Dually π_k(HA ∧^L Σ^∞K) ≅ H̃_k(K; A).
hypotheses: K a pointed simplicial set (cohomology of its realisation).
proofSteps: Σ^k HA ≅ sh^k HA in SHC (λ^k is a π̂_*-isomorphism since HA is semistable); sh^k HA is an Ω-spectrum with level 0 equal to A[S^k]; SHC(Σ^∞K, sh^k HA) ≅ [K, A[S^k]] (Schwede II Examples 1.17–1.18, API homSuspensionSpectrumEquiv of H.5:spectra/stable-homotopy-category); [K, A[S^k]] ≅ H̃^k(K; A) (H.3/cohomology-representability) (Schwede II Prop. 6.23).

For homology use the separate gap Stable homology comparison for Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectra: establish the stable comparison between HA ∧ᴸ Σ^∞K and the free simplicial A-module construction, including disconnected pointed K, then apply Moore/Dold–Thom and suspension in homology. Schwede II Proposition 6.23 does not supply this proof in the version read.
acceptance: For X a point, [Σ^∞_+ pt, Σ^k HA] = A for k = 0 and 0 otherwise.
H^1(S¹; ℤ) = ℤ via [Σ^∞_+S¹, ΣHℤ].

nodes.title: Connective covers and Postnikov sections of spectra
nodes.statement: For every n ∈ ℤ, the inclusion of (n−1)-connected spectra into SHC has a right adjoint X ↦ τ_{≥n}X = X⟨n⟩ (the (n−1)-connected cover, counit q_n : X⟨n⟩ → X) and the inclusion of (n+1)-coconnected spectra (π_k = 0 for k > n) has a left adjoint X ↦ τ_{≤n}X = P_n X (unit p_n); there is a unique δ making X⟨n+1⟩ → X → P_n X → ΣX⟨n+1⟩ a distinguished triangle, with π_k(X⟨n⟩) = π_k X for k ≥ n and 0 below, π_k(P_n X) = π_k X for k ≤ n and 0 above. X is the homotopy colimit of the covers as n → −∞. The pair (connective, coconnective) is a t-structure on SHC with heart equivalent to abelian groups via π₀ and H.
hypotheses: Functoriality in SHC (not on the point-set level); point-set functorial models via the positive model structure are not needed here.
proofSteps: Construct the cover by cellular approximation of [−, X] on {S^k}_{k≥n} (H.5:spectra/cellular-approximation, Schwede II Prop. 5.14), which is (n−1)-connected by H.5:spectra/connective-generation (Prop. 5.21), and show [A, q_n] bijective for (n−1)-connected A (Theorem 8.1); the section is the cone (Theorem 8.3), using Prop. 5.24.
π_* computations and uniqueness of δ (Schwede II Lemma 5.27).

t-structure and heart: Schwede II Remark 5.26 and Theorem 5.25; instantiate Mathlib's Triangulated.TStructure with t.le n = spectra with π_k = 0 for k < −n (the essential image of τ_{≥−n}) and t.ge n = spectra with π_k = 0 for k > −n, so that t.le 0 is the connective spectra.
acceptance: For X = HZ ∨ Σ²HZ ∨ Σ^{−2}HZ, τ_{≥0}X ≅ HZ ∨ Σ²HZ and τ_{≤−1}X ≅ Σ^{−2}HZ (τ_{≥0}KU = ku is checked in RefinedTraceMethods:RT.4:topological, where KU and ku are built).
The connective cover of a connective spectrum is itself; P₀ of a connective X is Hπ₀X.
The connective cover must not silently erase negative K-groups: τ_{≥0} of nonconnective K-theory loses K_{<0}.

nodes.title: Sequential homotopy colimits of spectra
nodes.statement: For a sequence X₀ → X₁ → X₂ → ⋯ of spectra, the homotopy colimit (mapping telescope) hocolim X_n fits into a distinguished triangle ⊕X_n →(1 − shift) ⊕X_n → hocolim X_n → Σ⊕X_n; for every homological functor E that takes sums to sums (Schwede II Def. 5.4; for example π_k) the map colim E(X_n) → E(hocolim X_n) is an isomorphism, and for cohomological E that takes countable sums to products there is the Milnor sequence 0 → lim¹ E(ΣX_n) → E(hocolim X_n) → lim E(X_n) → 0. On the point-set level the telescope of symmetric spectra computes it.
hypotheses: Countable sequences; SHC has countable sums (wedges).

The homological functor preserves countable sums; the cohomological functor sends countable sums to products. Without the latter the asserted Milnor sequence need not follow from the defining triangle.
proofSteps: Define the homotopy colimit in the triangulated category with sums (Schwede II Definition 5.3); colimit property of homological functors and Milnor sequence for cohomological ones taking countable sums to products (Schwede II Lemma 5.6, (5.7)–(5.8)).
Point-set telescope: Schwede II Proposition 5.11 and I Example 2.21.
acceptance: π_k commutes with sequential homotopy colimits (Schwede II Corollary 5.10).
X ≃ hocolim of its connective covers X⟨n⟩ as n → −∞ (H.5:spectra/postnikov-sections).

sources.locator: Chapter II, Definition 5.3 and Lemma 5.6, pp. 256–258 (PDF 257–259)

nodes.title: Cellular approximation in triangulated categories with sums
nodes.statement: Let T be a triangulated category with infinite sums, C a set of compact objects and ⟨C⟩⁺ the smallest class containing C and closed under sums and extensions to the right. For every cohomological functor E : T^op → Ab (taking sums to products) there are R ∈ ⟨C⟩⁺ and u ∈ E(R) such that f ↦ E(f)(u) is a bijection [G, R] → E(G) for every G ∈ C.
hypotheses: T triangulated with infinite sums (SHC: Schwede II Prop. 1.10); objects of C compact (S is compact, Schwede II Prop. 5.2).
proofSteps: Build R as a homotopy colimit of R₀ → R₁ → ⋯ where R₀ is a sum of objects of C and R_{n+1} kills the kernel of ev_u on [G, R_n] (Schwede II proof of Prop. 5.14), using Lemma 5.6 for maps out of compact objects and the Milnor sequence for E.
acceptance: For C = {S^k}_{k≥n} and E = SHC(−, X) this gives the (n−1)-connected cover (Schwede II Thm. 8.1).

sources.match: Schwede's Proposition 5.14.

nodes.title: Connective spectra are generated by spheres
nodes.statement: For n ∈ ℤ, the smallest class ⟨Sⁿ⟩⁺ of objects of SHC containing Sⁿ and closed under sums and extensions to the right (A, B in the class and A → B → C → ΣA distinguished ⇒ C in the class) is the class of (n−1)-connected spectra (true homotopy groups vanish below n).
hypotheses: Connectivity is measured with true homotopy groups.
proofSteps: (n−1)-connected spectra contain Sⁿ and are closed under sums and extensions to the right (long exact sequence of true homotopy groups).
Conversely apply H.5:spectra/cellular-approximation to [−, X] with C = {S^k}_{k≥n}; the resulting R → X is a π_*-isomorphism, hence an isomorphism in SHC (Schwede II Prop. 5.21).
acceptance: n = 0: a spectrum is connective iff it lies in ⟨S⟩⁺.
HA ∈ ⟨S⟩⁺ for every abelian group A.

nodes.title: Connective spectra are sequences of deloopings
nodes.statement: A connective levelwise Kan symmetric Ω-spectrum determines the sequence (|X_i|, σ̃_i). Conversely, apply Sing levelwise to a sequence of pointed CW spaces with π_j(X_i) = 0 for 0 ≤ j < i and weak equivalences X_i → ΩX_{i+1}, take a cofibrant replacement as a Bousfield–Friedlander spectrum, apply the left adjoint V, then take a stably fibrant replacement. The derived adjunction LV ⊣ RU (U forgets the symmetric actions) is the Quillen equivalence of Hovey–Shipley–Smith Theorem 4.3.2. These derived functors identify connective SHC with the homotopy category of connective sequential Ω-spectra; π_k X ≅ π_{k+i} X_i whenever k+i ≥ 0. EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:spectra-comparison supplies the comparison with Bhatt–Scholze’s ∞-category.
hypotheses: Pointed spaces of CW homotopy type; 'i-connected' in Bhatt–Scholze's convention means π_j = 0 for j < i (their footnote 29).
proofSteps: Bhatt–Scholze define connective spectra as the limit of S_* ←Ω S_*^{≥1} ←Ω ⋯ (Definition 12.8); the strict model is the Ω-spectrum (H.5:spectra/omega-spectra-and-eilenberg-maclane) with symmetric structure supplied by the Quillen equivalence V ⊣ U between symmetric and Bousfield–Friedlander spectra (Hovey–Shipley–Smith Thm. 4.3.2; packet gap 'Sequential versus symmetric spectra').
Connectivity of the levels is equivalent to connectivity of the spectrum for Ω-spectra.
acceptance: The connective Ω-model of Waldhausen K-theory has zeroth space Ω|wS.C| and positive levels |wS^{(n)}C| for n ≥ 1 (H.5:S-delooping/iterated-S-construction-omega-spectrum).
HA corresponds to (K(A, i))_i.

sources.match: Bhatt–Scholze's definition of connective spectra via deloopings.

nodes.title: Grouplike E∞-monoids are connective spectra
nodes.statement: Segal's machine X ↦ (X, BX, B²X, …) (H.4/segal-delooping-theorem) gives an equivalence between the homotopy theory of grouplike special Γ-spaces (grouplike E∞-monoids) and that of connective spectra, inverse to taking the underlying infinite loop space with its E∞-structure; any two such equivalences agree (May–Thomason).
hypotheses: Model: grouplike special Γ-spaces (H.4/gamma-space) with the stable Bousfield–Friedlander structure, and connective symmetric spectra (Γ-spaces evaluated on spheres, Schwede I p. 21); the statement is an equivalence of homotopy categories; proofs quoted: Segal 1974 Proposition 3.4, Lurie HA 5.2.6.10, May–Thomason 1978 (not read; packet gap 'Infinite loop space machine equivalence').
proofSteps: Segal's construction lands in connective Ω-spectra by H.4/segal-delooping-theorem; the inverse uses that every connective spectrum has a canonical E∞-monoid structure, which Bhatt–Scholze obtain from the ∞-categorical statement Mon_{E∞}(Sp^{≥0}) ≃ Sp^{≥0} (HA Lemma 1.1.2.10; quoted, packet gap 'Infinite loop space machine equivalence'); H.5:spectra/finite-biproducts gives only the homotopy-category consequence that π₀ is a group.
acceptance: The Γ-space of an abelian group A corresponds to HA.
N(Fin) (finite sets) is not grouplike (π₀ = ℕ); its group completion ΩB N(Fin) corresponds to the sphere spectrum (Barratt–Priddy–Quillen).

sources.match: Bhatt–Scholze's Theorem 12.9 (Segal; Lurie), with May–Thomason uniqueness.

nodes.title: Picard groupoids are 1-truncated connective spectra
nodes.statement: For a Picard groupoid C (symmetric monoidal groupoid with all objects invertible), the spectrum K(C) associated with the grouplike E∞-monoid N(C) has underlying space |N(C)|, π₀ K(C) = C/≅, π₁ K(C) = Aut(1) and π_k = 0 otherwise; this gives an equivalence between Picard groupoids (with symmetric monoidal functors and monoidal natural isomorphisms) and 1-truncated connective spectra.
hypotheses: C Picard; equivalence at the level of homotopy 2-categories / homotopy theories; Patel's comparison [Pat12, §3] quoted (packet gap 'Picard groupoids versus 1-truncated spectra').
proofSteps: N(C) is grouplike (H.4/picard-groupoid-grouplike) and 1-truncated (H.1/groupoid-nerve-one-type), so K(C) = Segal spectrum of N(C) is connective with π_k = 0 for k ≥ 2 (H.5:spectra/grouplike-einfty-connective-spectra).
The equivalence identifies both sides with grouplike E∞-monoids in groupoids (Bhatt–Scholze p. 59, citing Patel).
acceptance: Pic^ℤ(R) gives the 1-truncated spectrum with π₀ = Pic(R) × H⁰(Spec R, ℤ), π₁ = R^×.
The stable symmetric structure on Pic^ℤ(R) involves the sign (−1)^{fg} (Bhatt–Scholze Example 12.2(iii)).

sources.locator: Appendix §12, after the proof of Proposition 12.15, p. 59
sources.match: Bhatt–Scholze's statement, citing Patel §3 (as recorded in the paper extraction).

nodes.title: The K-theory symmetric spectrum of a Waldhausen category
nodes.statement: For a small Waldhausen category C (with chosen zero object, cofibrations and weak equivalences), the K-theory spectrum K(C) is the symmetric spectrum with n-th level the pointed simplicial set K(C)_n = diag N_· wS_·^{{1,…,n}}C (the diagonal of the (n+1)-fold simplicial nerve of weak equivalences of the cubical S-construction), whose realisation is |wS^{(n)}C|, Σ_n permuting the n directions, and structure maps σ_n : K(C)_n ∧ S¹ → K(C)_{n+1} induced by the inclusion of 1-simplices (S₁C ≅ C). Its zeroth level is the nerve of wC (not group-completed).
hypotheses: C a small Waldhausen category (GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction/waldhausen-categories); the S^Q-construction with the cube conditions of Schwede I Example 3.50.
proofSteps: Define S^Q_n C for finite sets Q as functors from the arrow category of [n]^Q satisfying the zero, cofibration-cube and pushout conditions (Schwede I Example 3.50); a choice of ordering of Q identifies it with the iterated S-construction.
The Σ_n-action permutes Q = {1, …, n}; the structure maps come from S₁C = C and the realisation of the multisimplicial set (H.2/simplicial-space-realisation, H.2/bisimplicial-realization-lemma).
acceptance: For C = finite pointed sets with injections as cofibrations, K(C) ≃ S (Barratt–Priddy–Quillen–Segal).
For an exact category with isomorphisms as weak equivalences, Ω|iS.C| ≃ ΩBQC (Waldhausen 1.9, via GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction/iS-versus-Q).

sources.match: Schwede's levels K(C)_n and Σ_n-actions via the S^Q-construction; the structure maps (left as [...] in Schwede) and the iso S^Q ≅ S^{Q−P}S^P ([define]) are packet-authored, from the inclusion of 1-simplices S₁C = C (Weibel IV Remark 8.3.2).

nodes.title: The iterated S.-construction is a connective Ω-spectrum
nodes.statement: For a small Waldhausen category C (K(C) = Ω|wS.C| and K_i(C) = π_{i+1}|wS.C| as in GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction), the K-theory symmetric spectrum (H.5:S-delooping/k-theory-symmetric-spectrum) is, from level 1 on, an Ω-spectrum: |wS^{(n)}C| → Ω|wS^{(n+1)}C| is a weak homotopy equivalence for n ≥ 1, using the deloopings supplied by GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction. It is semistable (positive Ω-spectra have stabilising homotopy groups, Schwede I Proposition 8.26(i) and Example 8.27), so its naive and true homotopy groups agree; hence its true homotopy groups are π_i K(C) = π_{i+1}|wS.C| = K_i(C) for i ≥ 0 and 0 for i < 0. The biexact pairing K(A) ∧ K(B) → K(C) is not part of this node; it is owned by GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.7, which consumes the smash product of H.5:spectra.
hypotheses: C small Waldhausen category; the S.-construction, additivity, the relative S.-fibration and the delooping |wS^{(n)}C| ≃ Ω|wS^{(n+1)}C| are supplied by GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction (requested).
proofSteps: π₁|wS.C| ≅ K₀(C) and K_i(C) = π_{i+1}|wS.C| are GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction/K-theory-space-of-a-waldhausen-category (Weibel IV 8.4, 8.5).
The deloopings |wS.ⁿC| ≃ Ω|wS.ⁿ⁺¹C| for n ≥ 1 are those of GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4/delooping-and-the-spectrum (Weibel V 1.7).

Compatibility: for a simplicial pointed space Y. with Y₀ = ∗ and its augmented, contractible path object PY., the map |Y₁| → Ω|Y.| adjoint to the 1-skeleton inclusion ΣY₁ ⊆ |Y.| (Weibel IV Remark 8.3.2) is homotopic to the fibre inclusion |Y₁| = |(PY)₀| → hofib(|PY.| → |Y.|) ≃ Ω|Y.|; apply this to Y. = wS.^{n+1}C in the last direction, after identifying S^{{1,…,n+1}}C with S.S^{{1,…,n}}C by ordering (Schwede I Example 3.50). So the adjoint structure maps of level n ≥ 1 are the supplied deloopings.

Assemble: an Ω-spectrum from level 1 has π_i = π_{i+1} of level 1 for i ≥ 0 (H.5:spectra/omega-spectra-and-eilenberg-maclane), it is semistable (Schwede I Proposition 8.26(i), Example 8.27; H.5:spectra/semistable), and it is connective since level n is (n−1)-connected.
acceptance: For an exact category A with isomorphisms as weak equivalences, |iS.A| ≃ BQA (Waldhausen 1.9; Weibel IV Exercises 8.5–8.6; GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction/iS-versus-Q).
Relative groups end with K₀(B) → K₀(C) → K₋₁(f) → 0 (Weibel IV Exercise 8.11).
A sequence of spaces without the fibration theorem does not count as the spectrum.

nodes.title: Functoriality and homotopy invariance of the K-theory spectrum
nodes.statement: Exact functors F : C → D induce maps of K-theory spectra, strictly functorially; a natural weak equivalence F ⇒ F′ of exact functors induces a homotopy (in the stable homotopy category, equality) K(F) = K(F′); an exact equivalence of Waldhausen categories induces a stable equivalence. The assembly is compatible with the sequential model (Weibel IV 8.5.5) and, for an exact category A with isomorphisms as weak equivalences, Ω of level 1 is naturally homotopy equivalent to ΩBQA (GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction/iS-versus-Q).
hypotheses: Exact functors between small Waldhausen categories; natural weak equivalences (pointwise in w).
proofSteps: Functoriality of S^Q and of realisation; a natural weak equivalence gives a functor C × [1] → w-morphisms, hence a homotopy of realisations levelwise (H.1/natural-transformations-adjoints-contractibility applied in the w-direction).
Exact equivalences have exact inverses up to natural isomorphism.
acceptance: The identity functor induces the identity.
Weibel IV Exercises 8.5–8.6 compare with BQ.

nodes.title: Moore spectra S/m
nodes.statement: For an integer m ≥ 1, the mod-m Moore spectrum S/m is the mapping cone of m : S → S (multiplication by m on the sphere spectrum), with the distinguished triangle S →m S → S/m →δ S¹. It is a connective Moore spectrum for ℤ/m: H₀(S/m; ℤ) = ℤ/m and H_k = 0 otherwise; π₀(S/m) = ℤ/m. S/m is well defined up to (non-unique) isomorphism as a cone of m (TR1, TR3). Every homomorphism ℤ/m → ℤ/m′ is realised by a morphism S/m → S/m′ (the exact sequence (6.42) applied to the defining triangle), uniquely when m or m′ is odd (the indeterminacy is Ext(ℤ/m, ℤ/m′ ⊗ ℤ/2) ≅ ℤ/gcd(2, m, m′)); uniqueness of Moore spectra for arbitrary groups (Schwede II Theorem 6.43) needs the spectrum Hurewicz theorem and is not used in this stage.
hypotheses: m ≥ 1; the point-set model is the mapping cone of a representative of m (for example a degree-m map from a subdivided simplicial circle to a Kan model of S¹, on level 1 of the free spectrum), well defined up to isomorphism in SHC.
proofSteps: Define S/m as the mapping cone (H.5:spectra/mapping-cone-and-homotopy-fibre) of m · id_S (Schwede II Definition 6.33 and the triangle in Remark/Example around Proposition 6.48).
Homology: the long exact sequence in HZ-homology gives H₀ = ℤ/m, others zero.

Limited functoriality: realise homomorphisms through the exact sequence (6.42) for maps out of S/m (Schwede II Construction 6.39 and the proof of Theorem 6.43); the indeterminacy is Ext(ℤ/m, π₁(S/m′)) = Ext(ℤ/m, ℤ/m′ ⊗ ℤ/2), zero for m′ odd (Remark 6.44).
acceptance: π₂(S/2) ≅ ℤ/4 (Schwede II Proposition 6.48), so S/2 is not a ring spectrum and 2 · id_{S/2} ≠ 0.
S/1 is stably trivial.

sources.locator: Chapter II, Definition 6.33, p. 284 (PDF 285); Construction 6.39, (6.41)–(6.42) and Theorem 6.43, pp. 285–286 (PDF 286–287); Proposition 6.48 and (6.50), pp. 287–288 (PDF 288–289)

nodes.title: Spectra with finite coefficients E/m
nodes.statement: For a spectrum E and m ≥ 1, E/m := E ∧^L S/m, an exact functor of E, which is a cofibre of m : E → E: the triangle E →m E → E/m →β ΣE (the defining triangle of S/m smashed with E) is distinguished; the mod-m homotopy groups are π_n(E; ℤ/m) := π_n(E/m) for all n ∈ ℤ, natural in E. For an Ω-spectrum E, π_n(E; ℤ/m) = colim_r π_{n+r}(E_r; ℤ/m) with Weibel's space-level groups [P^{n+r}(ℤ/m), E_r].
hypotheses: E any spectrum (no connectivity assumption; negative degrees included).
proofSteps: Define E/m := E ∧^L S/m (H.5:spectra/derived-smash-product); smashing the defining triangle of S/m with E is distinguished by exactness of ∧^L, so E/m is a mapping cone of m · 𝟙_E (H.5:spectra/mapping-cone-and-homotopy-fibre).

Compare with Weibel's colimit formula (Weibel IV 2.3.1) through the Ω-spectrum levels, using that F(S/m, S) ≅ Σ^{−1}S/m (apply the exact functor F(−, S) to the defining triangle; F(S, S) = S), so [Σ^{n−1}S/m, E] ≅ π_n(E ∧ S/m).
acceptance: (HA)/m has π₀ = A/m and π₁ = A[m].
K(R)/m defines K_n(R; ℤ/m) (Weibel IV Definition 2.4).

nodes.title: The Bockstein long exact sequence
nodes.statement: For every spectrum E and m ≥ 1 there is a natural long exact sequence ⋯ → π_n E →m π_n E → π_n(E; ℤ/m) →β π_{n−1} E →m π_{n−1} E → ⋯ in all degrees n ∈ ℤ, where β is induced by the connecting map E/m → ΣE.
hypotheses: Any spectrum E.
proofSteps: Apply the long exact sequence of the triangle E →m E → E/m → ΣE (H.5:spectra/cofibre-long-exact-sequence; Weibel IV 2.1.1 for spaces via the cofibration S^{n−1} →ℓ S^{n−1} → P^n).
acceptance: For E = S, m = 2: π₁ S →2 π₁ S is zero (π₁ S = ℤ/2), giving 0 → π₂(S) ⊗ ℤ/2 = ℤ/2 → π₂(S/2) → π₁(S)[2] = ℤ/2 → 0 (H.6/mod-l-homotopy-and-bockstein-sequence).
Naturality in E commutes with the connecting maps.

sources.locator: 2.1.1 and Universal Coefficient Sequence 2.2, p. IV.18

nodes.title: The universal coefficient sequence for mod-m homotopy
nodes.statement: For every spectrum E, m ≥ 1 and n ∈ ℤ there is a natural short exact sequence 0 → π_n(E) ⊗ ℤ/m → π_n(E; ℤ/m) → π_{n−1}(E)[m] → 0, where A[m] is the m-torsion subgroup. It is not split in general: for m = 2, π₂(S; ℤ/2) = π₂(S/2) ≅ ℤ/4 (the splitting for m odd or 4 | m is H.6/uct-splitting). For K-theory: 0 → K_n(C) ⊗ ℤ/m → K_n(C; ℤ/m) → K_{n−1}(C)[m] → 0.
hypotheses: Any spectrum E and m ≥ 1, all n ∈ ℤ. (Weibel's space-level version 2.2 has modulus ℓ and needs degree ≥ 3.)
proofSteps: Extract the short exact sequence from H.6/bockstein-long-exact-sequence: coker(m) = π_n ⊗ ℤ/m and ker(m) = π_{n−1}[m] (Weibel IV 2.2).
Non-splitting for m = 2 from π₂(S/2) = ℤ/4 (Schwede II Proposition 6.48; Weibel IV Example 2.2.1).
acceptance: Nonsplit example: π_{m+2}(S^m; ℤ/2) = ℤ/4 for m ≥ 3 and π₂(BO; ℤ/2) = ℤ/4 (Weibel IV Example 2.2.1).
K₂(ℤ; ℤ/2) ≅ ℤ/4 has a nonzero torsion right-hand term (Weibel IV Example 2.5.1).
The Bott element in K₂(R; ℤ/ℓ) depends on the chosen splitting (Weibel IV Remark 2.5.3).

sources.locator: Definition 2.1, 2.1.1, Universal Coefficient Sequence 2.2, Example 2.2.1, Proposition 2.3, 2.3.1, Definition 2.4, Theorem 2.5, Proposition 2.7, pp. IV.18–21

nodes.title: Non-natural splitting of the universal coefficient sequence for m odd or 4 | m
nodes.statement: If m is odd or divisible by 4, the universal coefficient sequence 0 → π_n(E) ⊗ ℤ/m → π_n(E; ℤ/m) → π_{n−1}(E)[m] → 0 of H.6/mod-l-homotopy-and-bockstein-sequence splits for every spectrum E and n ∈ ℤ; the splitting is not natural.
hypotheses: m odd or 4 | m. Quoted from F. Peterson via Browder [Br, 1.8], as cited by Weibel (gap 'Peterson splitting').
proofSteps: For m = p an odd prime, π_*(E/p) is an F_p-vector space since p · id_{S/p} = 0 (Schwede II Example 6.45), so the sequence splits. The general case is Browder [Br, 1.8], not read.
acceptance: m = 2 is excluded: π₂(S/2) = ℤ/4 (H.6/moore-spectrum).
The splitting is not natural (Weibel IV Exercise 2.3).

nodes.title: Coprime decomposition of Moore spectra
nodes.statement: If m = q₁q₂ with gcd(q₁, q₂) = 1, the sum of maps S/q₁ → S/m and S/q₂ → S/m realising ℤ/q₁ → ℤ/m (multiplication by q₂) and ℤ/q₂ → ℤ/m (multiplication by q₁) is an isomorphism S/q₁ ∨ S/q₂ ≅ S/m in SHC; hence π_n(E; ℤ/m) ≅ π_n(E; ℤ/q₁) × π_n(E; ℤ/q₂) naturally in E.
hypotheses: q₁, q₂ coprime positive integers.
proofSteps: Realise the two inclusions by maps of defining triangles (H.6/moore-spectrum).

On π_* compare the universal coefficient sequences of S/q₁ ∨ S/q₂ and S/m: ℤ/q₁ × ℤ/q₂ ≅ ℤ/m and the torsion terms agree, so the five lemma applies (H.6/mod-l-homotopy-and-bockstein-sequence, H.5:spectra/finite-biproducts).

nodes.title: Transition maps between Moore spectra and the mod-p^r tower
nodes.statement: For a prime p and r ≥ 1 there are maps ι_r : S/p^r → S/p^{r+1} realising multiplication by p : ℤ/p^r → ℤ/p^{r+1} on H₀ and ρ_r : S/p^{r+1} → S/p^r realising the reduction ℤ/p^{r+1} → ℤ/p^r, fitting into maps of defining triangles (identity and p on the two sphere terms), compatible with the Bocksteins; they induce maps E/p^r → E/p^{r+1} and E/p^{r+1} → E/p^r and the tower ⋯ → E/p^{r+1} → E/p^r → ⋯ → E/p. On homotopy they give the maps of universal coefficient sequences induced by p : ℤ/p^r → ℤ/p^{r+1} and reduction.
hypotheses: p prime; the maps are chosen as maps of triangles (TR3), unique up to the indeterminacy of Moore-spectrum maps; for p odd the choices are canonical (2-divisibility).
proofSteps: Construct ι_r and ρ_r by the morphism-of-triangles axiom applied to (1, p) and (p, 1) on S →(p^r) S (H.5:spectra/triangulated-structure; Schwede II Theorem 9.9(iii) uses ψ_n : S/p^n → S/p^{n+1} realising p).
Naturality in E via ∧^L.
acceptance: ρ_r ∘ ι_r realises multiplication by p on S/p^r up to the indeterminacy.
The colimit of the ι_r is S/p^∞ (H.6/qp-zp-coefficients); the limit of the ρ_r defines p-completion (H.6/p-completion).

nodes.title: ℚ_p/ℤ_p coefficients and their universal coefficient sequence
nodes.statement: For a prime p let S/p^∞ = hocolim_r S/p^r along ι_r, a Moore spectrum for ℤ/p^∞ = ℚ_p/ℤ_p. For every spectrum E, E ∧^L S/p^∞ = hocolim_r E/p^r and there is a natural short exact sequence 0 → π_n(E) ⊗ ℚ_p/ℤ_p → π_n(E; ℚ_p/ℤ_p) → π_{n−1}(E){p} → 0, where A{p} is the p-power torsion; the connecting map is a Bockstein. If π_{n+1}(E) is finite then π_n(E){p} ≅ π_{n+1}(E; ℚ_p/ℤ_p).
hypotheses: p prime; sequential homotopy colimit in SHC.
proofSteps: π_* commutes with sequential homotopy colimits (H.5:spectra/sequential-homotopy-colimit); take the colimit of the universal coefficient sequences: ι_r is induced by the identity on the source sphere and multiplication by p on the target sphere of p^r, so it acts by multiplication by p on the terms π_n(E) ⊗ ℤ/p^r and by the inclusions π_{n−1}(E)[p^r] ⊆ π_{n−1}(E)[p^{r+1}] on the torsion terms, with colimits π_n(E) ⊗ ℚ_p/ℤ_p and π_{n−1}(E){p}; filtered colimits of abelian groups are exact (Mathlib).
The finiteness consequence: if π_{n+1} E is finite then π_{n+1}E ⊗ ℚ_p/ℤ_p = 0.
acceptance: For E = HZ, E ∧ S/p^∞ ≃ H(ℚ_p/ℤ_p): π₀ = ℚ_p/ℤ_p and π₁ = 0 since ℤ has no p-torsion; for E = S, π₀(S/p^∞) = ℚ_p/ℤ_p.
K_n(R){ℓ} ≅ K_{n+1}(R; ℚ_ℓ/ℤ_ℓ) when K_{n+1}(R) is finite (ArithmeticKTheory request).

nodes.title: Homotopy limits of towers of spectra
nodes.statement: For a tower ⋯ → X₂ → X₁ → X₀ in SHC, a homotopy limit holim X_r is an object with compatible maps to the X_r fitting into a distinguished triangle holim X_r → ∏_r X_r →(1 − shift) ∏_r X_r → Σ holim X_r; it exists, is unique up to non-unique isomorphism, and on the point-set level is computed by the limit of a tower of fibrations between stably fibrant spectra. Maps of towers induce maps of homotopy limits (not uniquely in general).
hypotheses: Countable products exist in SHC (H.5:spectra/shc-products); point-set model via stable fibrant replacement (H.5:spectra/stable-model-structure).
proofSteps: Dualise Schwede II Definition 5.3 (homotopy colimits) using products; existence from countable products and the octahedral axiom (H.5:spectra/triangulated-structure).

Point-set model: replace the tower by a tower of stable fibrations between stably fibrant spectra and take the levelwise limit; that it represents the homotopy limit is the standard comparison for towers of fibrations, not in the sources read (point-set products of stably fibrant spectra represent SHC products by the proof of Schwede II Proposition 1.10(ii); Schwede II p. 297 uses holim of the Postnikov tower without defining it).
acceptance: holim of a constant tower with identity maps is X.
X ≃ holim P_n X for the Postnikov tower (H.5:spectra/postnikov-sections).

sources.locator: Chapter II, Definition 5.3, p. 256 (PDF 257); proof of Theorem 8.3, p. 297 (PDF 298)

nodes.title: The Milnor lim¹ sequence for homotopy limits of towers
nodes.statement: For a tower X of spectra and k ∈ ℤ there is a natural short exact sequence 0 → lim¹_r π_{k+1}(X_r) → π_k(holim X_r) → lim_r π_k(X_r) → 0, where lim and lim¹ are the inverse limit and its first derived functor for towers of abelian groups (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1). If the tower π_{k+1}(X_r) is Mittag-Leffler (for example finite groups, or surjective transition maps) then π_k(holim X_r) ≅ lim_r π_k(X_r). Natural for maps of towers, with respect to any induced map of homotopy limits that is part of a morphism of the defining triangles.
hypotheses: Countable towers; lim¹ of towers of abelian groups and its Mittag-Leffler vanishing imported from ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1 (requested).
proofSteps: Apply π_k (which commutes with products) to the defining triangle holim → ∏X_r →(1−shift) ∏X_r; the kernel and cokernel of 1 − shift on ∏π are lim and lim¹ (dual of Schwede II Lemma 5.6 and Remark 5.9; used on p. 298).
Mittag-Leffler vanishing: ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1/mittag-leffler and /mittag-leffler-lim-one (with Mathlib's IsMittagLeffler for the set-level condition).
acceptance: Finite groups: lim¹ = 0, so π_k(holim) = lim π_k.
Exhibit a tower with nonzero lim¹ (H.6/nonzero-lim-one-example).

For a tower of cochain complexes K_n with degreewise surjective transitions, the Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectra H(K_n) (H.5:spectra/eilenberg-maclane-of-chain-complex, π_k = H^{−k}) have holim H(K_n) ≅ H(lim K_n), and this node's sequence for k = −p agrees with ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1/milnor-sequence (comparison only; complexes are not identified with all spectra).

nodes.title: A tower with nonzero lim¹
nodes.statement: For a prime p, the tower ⋯ →p S →p S →p S of sphere spectra (multiplication by p) has lim_r π₀(X_r) = lim(⋯ →p ℤ →p ℤ) = 0 and lim¹(⋯ →p ℤ →p ℤ) ≅ ℤ_p/ℤ ≠ 0, so π_{−1}(holim) ≅ ℤ_p/ℤ, which is uncountable, although every term has π_{−1} = 0. Hence homotopy limits cannot be replaced by inverse limits of homotopy groups without a Mittag-Leffler hypothesis.
hypotheses: p prime.
proofSteps: The tower ⋯ →p ℤ →p ℤ has lim = 0 and lim¹ = coker(∏ℤ →(1−p·shift) ∏ℤ) ≅ ℤ_p/ℤ (standard computation via the short exact sequence of towers 0 → p^rℤ → ℤ → ℤ/p^r → 0 and lim of ℤ/p^r = ℤ_p (Mathlib PadicInt.lift and PadicInt.toZModPow), using ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1/lim-one-six-term).
Apply H.6/milnor-sequence with k = −1: π_{−1}(holim) ≅ lim¹ π₀ = ℤ_p/ℤ.
acceptance: This realises the roadmap's acceptance test asking for a tower whose derived-limit obstruction is nonzero.

sources.match: Schwede notes that the lim¹ term can be nonzero (the example is a '[...]' placeholder in this draft); the tower used here is packet-authored.

nodes.title: p-completion of spectra
nodes.statement: For a prime p and a spectrum E, the p-completion is E^∧_p := F(S/p^∞, ΣE) with the natural map E → E^∧_p adjoint to Id ∧ δ : E ∧^L S/p^∞ → ΣE (Schwede II §9.3); it is a homotopy limit of the tower E/p^r along the reduction maps (H.6/moore-spectrum-change-of-coefficients; Schwede II Theorem 9.9(iii), Remark 9.11). E is p-complete if E → E^∧_p is an isomorphism. p-completion is exact, and E^∧_p is p-local.
hypotheses: Internal Hom F(−, −) of SHC (H.5:spectra/derived-smash-product); the homotopy limit is that of the specific tower E/p^r with reduction maps dual to the maps ψ_n used to form S/p^∞.
proofSteps: Define E^∧_p := F(S/p^∞, ΣE) with S/p^∞ from H.6/qp-zp-coefficients; it is exact and functorial since F(−, −) is.

F(S/p^n, S) ≅ Σ^{−1}S/p^n by applying F(−, S) to the defining triangle; under this the dual of ψ_n realises the reduction ρ_n, so F(S/p^∞, ΣE) is a homotopy limit of F(S/p^n, ΣE) ≅ E/p^n (Schwede II Theorem 9.9(iii) and Remark 9.11; H.6/homotopy-limit-of-tower). For p odd the reduction maps are unique (their indeterminacy Ext(ℤ/p^{n+1}, π₁(S/p^n)) vanishes); for p = 2 use the ρ_n dual to the chosen ψ_n.
Weibel IV 2.9 defines the ℓ-adic completion as the homotopy limit of E ∧ P^∞(ℤ/ℓ^ν).
acceptance: S^∧_p has π₀ = ℤ_p.
H(ℤ/p) is p-complete; HQ^∧_p = 0.
